summary: One medium handoff finding, not a mathematical correction to the extraction. All 54 items were checked against the four-page published paper and its explicit inputs; the six library statuses are supported by declarations read at the pins, and the 48 missing items are routed exactly once. The prime-three exception, fixed-point weights and BGS/Vieta convention bridge are sound. However, four accepted papers now target the same Part II: the actual queue generator emits four design jobs and four review jobs with the same respective IDs, while its single prompt retains only the last paper's brief. Martin's complete 35-item Part II brief is lost on regeneration. The live design issue still has Martin's original brief, so this is not a claim that its published instructions have already lost that material.
checked: Independence: extraction by Codex codex-c83e7a and review by Claude Code cc-fb70e5; this red team is Codex codex-a71f92 and did neither. Read the result, report and independent review in full at repository snapshot 0ba46f9a37abb04b3b436c797818417fa8bab41b. Preflight f1491f30e3b171fab8bd8bb2542492b61ba04e9e changes neither the target nor the queue generator or the four relevant accepted paper routes.

Freshly retrieved and read all four published pages, 623–626, of Martin's DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01346-9 on 2026-09-24. PDF SHA-256 3e1f4b7f99f18b71159463aaf2d9e649e11317272782f9105299a9d72369097c matches the extraction. Rendered pp.624–625 to check every branch of (2.1), the theorem wording, fixed-point prose and (2.2)–(2.5).

Complete inventory: 54 unique IDs, six library and 48 missing, no planned claims; all 48 missing IDs occur in exactly one route, 13 to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4 and 35 to ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIMarkoff. The five displays in section 2, all three theorems and the conjecture are represented. The conjecture remains a proposition, not an asserted proof.

Items 1–13: coefficient-three equation, exclusion of the origin rather than every zero coordinate, integral Vieta involutions, preservation and positivity, sorted descent, the unique descending move, acyclicity by a height maximum, and reduction through the positive root orbit. Independently checked the descent inequalities and 22 exact positive integer examples; no primitivity assumption is substituted for the reduction argument.

Items 14–35 and 54: Vieta subgroup versus the group also generated by coordinate permutations, loop deletion only for simple-graph reachability, at-most-one-zero-coordinate over a field, all weight branches, complementary weights including fixed points, invariant-set sum reindexing and cardinality cancellation. Permutations normalize the Vieta subgroup and fix (1,1,1), which proves equality of the two root orbits and the equivalence of transitivity and Vieta connectivity.

Items 31–34: p=2 has four vertices and fixed moves; p=3 has eight vertices with independent sign-flip moves, so only the latter prime violates the printed divisibility statement. The extraction already corrects this to p≠3. Existing confirmed errata PAPER-MARTIN-25/E1 records the issue; E2–E3 are preprint mistakes already corrected in the published version. Absence of an inline sourceIssues list in this older extraction is not an unrecorded-erratum finding.

Fresh BGS arXiv:1607.01530v1, pp.1–5, SHA-256 50f3dcde0c4a3a841f4eb3556838ecd162a7988ea3d3c1235f53c9c427b03e9e: Theorems 1–2 concern Γ generated by mutations and permutations, not the larger double-sign-change group Δ. The giant-orbit bound is ≤p^ε and the exceptional-prime bound is ≤T^ε for sufficiently large parameters. The extraction uses these correctly and does not assume that every giant Γ-orbit is already one Vieta component.

Items 36–43 and 53: the noncircular order is elementary divisibility, BGS giant Γ-orbit with complement <p, Γ-transitivity, root-orbit comparison, Vieta connectivity, and lifting to positive triples. The strict giant-component consequence is used only after connectivity, and the sparse-prime estimate transfers through the all-prime connectivity equivalence.

Fresh Eddy–Fuchs–Litman–Martin–Tripeny author PDF, pp.1–4, SHA-256 0795f7cd9c28c147ed642392919cd0879714a36e461ca353b379f7ea66bee8c0: Definition 1.2, Theorem 1.4 and the graph-convention discussion match items 44–46. Exact multiplication of (863#)(53#)(13#)(7#)(5#)·3³·2⁵ gives a 393-digit integer beginning 344804838267768, strictly below 3489·10^389. The comparison uses integers, not floating-point rounding. The coefficient-one conjugacy requires p≠3. The publisher DOI returned 403 in this run, so the extraction's reported publisher-HTML decimal discrepancy was not independently reverified.

All six library items: read ZMod, ZMod.fintype, ZMod.card and its prime Field instance; SimpleGraph.Reachable, ConnectedComponent and ConnectedComponent.supp; reachable_fromEdgeSet_fromRel_eq_reflTransGen; the to_additive source of Fintype.sum_equiv; and ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff, at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Finset.sum_involution has a cancellation conclusion, not literally the named weight-balance statement. Both complete pinned Lean trees were searched for Markoff, Markov triples/equations/numbers and Penner with ignored files included; no specialized implementation was found at Mathlib or Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369.

Read reviewed coverage for DY.0, CA.0, CA.4, FF.0, FF.5 and AC.0, all seven ArithmeticDynamics stage descriptions and EffectiveDiophantineMethods stage descriptions. CA.4 is a defensible integer-descent owner; DY.0–DY.6 do not supply the affine three-involution endpoint; FF.5 is process, not an owner of a new theorem. The corrected arithmeticgeometry area and Part II title agree with the atlas.

Searched current atlas stage extracts, integrated decompositions, packets, link maps, restructuring proposals and new-roadmap definitions for specialized Markoff/Penner suppliers. Compared the four accepted routes from Chen, Gamburd–Magee–Ronan, Martin and Ghosh–Sarnak to the common Part II. Their shared destination is intentional; the later papers are no longer absent as they were when the original report was written. This is a routing comparison, not a full mathematical re-review of those three other papers.

Independent exhaustive regression for all 26 primes through 101: 76,224 nonzero vertices; every labelled mutation preserves the equation, is involutive and preserves nonzero points; all permutations preserve the carrier; the weights sum to one and are complementary on all moves for p>3, including fixed moves; every component has size divisible by p except p=3; component coordinate sums satisfy twice the sum equals the cardinality; scaling by 3 bijects the coefficient-three and coefficient-one carriers and intertwines moves for p≠3. Found 3,186 labelled fixed moves across all primes. All assertions passed. These are finite regression checks, not a proof for arbitrary primes.

Negative and degenerate tests: (0,1,2) over F5 has weights (0,3,3); (2,1,5) over F11 is fixed by the first move with weight 6; an empty invariant sum is zero; (2,0,0) over Z/4Z refutes extending the one-zero-coordinate assertion to arbitrary rings; scaling by 3 collapses all eight F3 vertices; maximal divisors of 12 below 6 are {4,6}.

Ran the actual make_queue.main in --dry-run mode, observing its return locals without patching production code. Four accepted Part II routes contain 13, 18, 35 and 5 item IDs in registry order. Regeneration produces four copies of DESIGN-ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIMarkoff and four of its review job. Only the Ghosh–Sarnak brief and its full item list survive in the final prompt. The report includes a reproducer and distinguishes this from live issue #1700, which still contains Martin's original brief.

Scope boundary: Martin's entire proof and the explicit prerequisite statements were checked; BGS's complete endgame/middle-game/opening proofs and Eddy et al.'s full threshold algorithm were not certified here. The extraction honestly assigns that decomposition to the design job. No Lean compilation or formalisation is claimed.

findings.claim: The accepted 35-item Martin Part II brief is not preserved by queue regeneration when the other accepted papers sharing this owner are present. The generator emits duplicate design/review job IDs and overwrites their single prompt with the last paper's brief instead of combining the accepted mathematical obligations. This is a downstream handoff defect, not a wrong mathematical route or a false statement in Martin's extraction.
findings.evidence: At snapshot 0ba46f9a37abb04b3b436c797818417fa8bab41b, accepted routes in registry order are PAPER-CHEN-24 route 2 (13 items), PAPER-GAMBURD-MAGEE-RONAN-19 route 2 (18), PAPER-MARTIN-25 route 2 (35), and PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22 route 5 (5), all with identical roadmap ID, parent, title and area. make_queue appends one design tuple per route and add assigns prompts[path] = prompt_text. A full actual --dry-run invocation produces four design records and four corresponding review records; the final prompt contains the complete Ghosh–Sarnak brief and its five IDs but none of the other three complete briefs. In particular, PAPER-MARTIN-25/20 and the instruction to build extended Penner weights are absent. Ghosh–Sarnak's prose says it coalesces with Martin, but the generator does not perform that combination. Live issue #1700 was separately read and still has Martin's original full brief; the claim is about reproducible regeneration, not an already overwritten live issue. The same generic shared-ID risk was noted for a different owner in REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23.md, section 4, and remains present in the inspected code.
findings.fix: Have the maintainer/fix job group accepted new/Part II routes by destination roadmap before creating design and review jobs. Validate matching parent, title and area; produce exactly one design and one review job; combine every accepted brief with its paper/route provenance and item IDs, preserving common-carrier instructions and convention distinctions. For this destination, preserve all 71 source-qualified item references from the four routes and Martin's p=3 regression, weight proof, BGS bridge and effective endpoint. Shared statements should be constructed once, not erased or assigned new owner IDs to dodge the collision. Add a regression using these four accepted routes asserting unique job IDs and preservation of all four briefs/item lists; regenerate the prompt and refresh the live design issue through the normal maintainer workflow. Do not rewrite the mathematically sound Martin inventory, remove the other sources or modify their accepted verdicts.
